cases.reason: The 2002 and 2023 formats are word for word the same, and the clause has no syntax or general rules of its own in either edition. The two operands it names are formats that are also word-identical: configuration-section (2002 12.2.1 against 2023 12.3.2, the same four optional paragraphs in the same order) and input-output-section (2002 12.3.1 against 2023 12.4.2, file-control and i-o-control). The 2002-only material under these operands (SOURCE-COMPUTER WITH DEBUGGING MODE, 2002 12.2.4.1) sits one level further down in a paragraph format that is a separate catalog rule and gets its own verdict; it does not change what this rule governs, which is the division header and the order of its two optional sections. The rule cannot govern a communication-section entry or a cd-name. The reader's evidence (l1c08 shapes and the section-order negative, run at --std 2002) covers that scope.

cases.reason: The reader checked use-statement (USE formats identical) but not the other meta-term the format names: 'sentence', which 2002 describes in 14.4, where a sentence is a sequence of procedural statements and the statements are identified in Table 13. 2002's Table 13 holds the communication statements DISABLE, ENABLE, PURGE, RECEIVE (conditional phrases NO DATA / WITH DATA) and SEND, whose operand is a cd-name, and CALL with the ON OVERFLOW conditional phrase. 2023's Table 12 (14.5.1) has none of DISABLE, ENABLE or PURGE, gives RECEIVE and SEND only the message-facility forms ([NOT] ON EXCEPTION), and has no CALL ON OVERFLOW. So the 2002 Format 1 and Format 2 admit, in a nondeclarative section, a paragraph and a declarative section, sentences that the 2023 format's 'sentence' does not, and the 2023 row's evidence shows none of them at --std 2002. The referenced clause changed (reader brief item 3), and the rule reaches statements whose operand is a cd-name. The probe shows the compiler correct at 2002: a Format 1 procedure division with PURGE in a declarative section, DISABLE/ENABLE in a section, and RECEIVE ... NO DATA ... END-RECEIVE, SEND and CALL ... ON OVERFLOW in a paragraph compiles and runs ('PDC RAN', exit 0, only the COBOL0903 obsolete warnings) at --std 2002, and is refused at --std 2023 (COBOL0902 for each communication construct, COBOL0882 for CALL ON OVERFLOW). Needs: a 2002 witness for sentences of the communication statements and CALL ON OVERFLOW inside the 2002 procedure division formats (this probe is a candidate). Class also fits deferral (14.4/Table 13 changed) and removed-form (CALL ON OVERFLOW).
